interference.method: bounding-box prefilter, OCC boolean common > 1 mm3; designed contacts excluded: tips/nozzles in the target place's labware, single-channel shafts in the target tube rack, the coupling halves meeting in a bay (balls/pins, stud/latch), the latch roller on the release-post ramp over its last 7 mm; Z sampled at 50, 85 and 100 % of each working stroke
found_and_fixed_in_pass_2: dock: with a 230 mm stroke the other carriage's tool and the gripper fingers hit the parked tools and release posts (clearance -104 mm): Z stroke 345, gantry +115 (beam mid z 545)

dock: the carriage plate (lowest fixed point z 190) sweeps any bay it crosses in Y: the dock row is entered at its right end (bays x -296..250, carriage travel to 465) and travelled along X; bays moved behind G so the plate clears the posts when the head works row G (axis y 472)

dock: bay pitch 78 (72 mm tool plates touched at 72); tools rest on cradle lugs, not on the tool plate (cradles are wider than the plate); release-post column moved in front of the eight-channel manifolds; latch tail +6 mm
TC-1 lid guide strip 15 mm further out (single-channel cradles at B1/C1 column 1 reach x -208.5); deck to x -270
tip parking TPK-1 swapped with the D2 plate stack (the 86.6 mm TPK-1 stood where eight-channel cradles pass at C1 column 12; K2 had assumed 50 mm)
G2/G3 frames recessed 7, G4 p1000 rack 75 (was 50), A2 rack 20 (was 15): eight-channel manifold cheeks at the next column
shaker at D4 sunk 40 mm on a tray (lid top was z 150: 40 mm under the carriage plate, below the 1.5 x rule; also takes the 44 mm wash plate with a lid)
gripper fingers checked open (gap 92); the head_l model shows them part-closed

design.height_note: the parked tool's plate top sits at stroke L_DOCK_S (z 307 global); bays stand on the dock base at deck level

design.release: a fixed steel post in front of the bay with a 45 deg ramp meets the latch roller in the last 7 mm of the carriage's descent and pushes the latch open; the latch closes by its spring as the carriage rises with a tool

design.drip: PA12 tray with an absorbent pad under each bay

clearance.rule: a tool parked at the bottom of the stroke hangs 289 mm (Hn) below its plate; while one carriage works in a bay, the other carriage (tool up, NO TIPS) and the gripper pass over the neighbouring bays: their lowest points must clear the parked tools and the release posts by >= 8 mm
clearance.consequence: pass 1 fails by about 90 mm: the other carriage's tool and the gripper fingers run into the neighbouring parked tools and posts.  Pass 2: Z stroke 345 and gantry +115 (beam mid z 545): nothing on the deck changes (same reach, same lowest fixed point z 190), the machine is 115 mm taller, the Z axes 115 mm longer, M1 grows (lever) and an exchange takes about 51 s instead of 26 s
planner_rules: no tips on EITHER carriage while the head is over the dock row (eject or park the idle carriage's tips first)
the dock row is entered and left at s 0 on all three axes; inside it only the exchanging carriage moves in Z

dock.entry_rule: enter and leave the dock row at its right end (xc >= 465), no tips on either carriage

coupling.orientation: two balls on an edge along Y (the nozzle row), one ball at +X
coupling.why_not_R50 (disagreement with the study: with R 50 the ball triangle spans 75 mm in X (edge along Y) or 87 mm (one ball forward): with the pin pairs (17 mm) the bracket is 92-104 mm wide, more than the 90 mm carriage pitch allows (two carriages side by side need about 10 mm between brackets).  R 36 gives a 72 mm bracket at 90 mm pitch.  Cost: moments need 1.39 x the preload of R 50, so P rises from 500 to 520 N and the eject pad is put within 15 mm of the axis (case B')
coupling.stud: pull stud at x +14 mm from the axis (the plunger pusher needs the axis): inside R/2 = 18: all three balls stay loaded

interface.nozzle: single nozzle or eight-nozzle row centre on the coupling axis (x 0, y -102.5 rel. the carriage axis) within 2 mm, row along Y
interface.nozzle_heights: two standard heights: tool-plate top to nozzle end Hn = 289.3 mm (p10/p200/p300 tools: nozzle at z 360 at the top) and 259.3 mm (p1000: z 390)
interface.plunger: each cradle brings its pipette's plunger button under a guided slider whose top pad sits 2 mm below the tool-plate top on the axis; the carriage pusher (0-35 mm stroke, >= 80 N) presses it through the bracket; different strokes are absorbed by the pusher's software stroke table and the contact switch (found per exchange); different pipette heights by the cradle's own V-block height, set so the slider pad and Hn are standard
interface.eject: cradle lever brings the pipette's ejector button to a pad under the eject pin (22 mm from the axis); the fixed finger on the head enters the bracket hole only in the eject over-travel (12 mm above s 0)
interface.force_switch: the cradle's disc-spring stack (set to that pipette's pick-up force) lifts the D3 push-rod through the tool plate to the D2F on the carriage
interface.code: four D4x2 magnets in the tool plate top, read through 1 mm of bracket by four Hall switches
interface.mass_and_width: <= 1.3 kg, <= 70 mm in X, centre of mass within 15 mm of the axis (study 3.2)

cradles.pattern: CB-1 (rev J) turned horizontal: ONE machined body per pipette = flange under the tool plate (4 x M4 from the tool-plate top, two D4 dowels: round at (-6, -70), slot at (36, -120), asymmetric so it fits one way only) + back plate with integral V-pads + two dock lugs (D6 round hole at x -20, slot at x +20, z -172..-162 below the tool-plate top: the standard bay interface); separate opposing-V straps (2 x M4 each); eight-channel tools add two 6 mm manifold cheeks below a notch in the back plate

A deep-well plate is often sealed with a mat instead: the gripper cannot place a mat: stay with lids

magnet.MB-1: does NOT suit: MB-1 holds 2 mm magnets in rows between the 0.2 mL wells (5.4 mm cones at 9 mm pitch) with the magnet top 5 mm above the well floor; square 8.2 mm (or round 7 mm) deep wells leave 0.8-2 mm between wells: no room for the rows
magnet.needed: a bought 96 deep-well magnet plate (ring or bar magnets around/under each well, SBS footprint, about 20-25 mm tall, the plate sitting in it) on the standard place: B2 gets it as a swap insert (4 screws), or B4 holds it and the low-elution magnet moves to a C-row place
magnet.pellet: with the wash volumes the liquid stands 5.7 mm (200 uL) above the floor in the square well: the magnet must pull the pellet within the lowest 5 mm of the side wall (or to the floor ring) so beads are not lost high in the well; bench rig: bead capture at 200 uL and at the elution volume

shaker.clamp: the bought shaker clamps the SBS skirt (bottom 6-7 mm): deep-well plates share the footprint and skirt: PASS if the maker lists deep-well plates (CONFIRM); its maximum load and speed for a 0.2 kg plate (CONFIRM)
